answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require every identity to lock a refundable stake in a shared bond pool, a reef of deposits that grows denser as more honest agents join. A newcomer starts small, like a walnut seed planted in an orchard: it bears fruit only after a record of verified work. Spinning up thousands of fake identities means funding thousands of stakes, and any identity caught cheating forfeits its bond, so attack cost scales linearly while honest participation stays cheap.
